etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: Possibly from Malay kampong, kampung (“group of buildings, village”), via Dutch or Portuguese, altered under the influence of Etymology 2. Doublet of kampung.
senses: An enclosure within which workers, prisoners, or soldiers are confined.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From Middle English compounen, from Middle French componre, compondre (“to put together”), from Latin componō, from Latin com- (“together”) + ponō (“to put”).
senses: (mathematics) Dealing with numbers of various denominations of quantity, or with processes more complex than the simple process.
Anything made by combining several things.
(transitive) To form (a resulting mixture) by combining different elements, ingredients, or parts; to mingle with something else.
(transitive, law) To settle by agreeing on less than the claim, or on different terms than those stipulated.
